The Flow Imaging Lab at Mudd works to mechanically recreate fish swimming behaviours and investigate their effects on fluid flow to optimize underwater vehicle systems. I worked on the "Fish-Inspired Propulsion through a Water-Air Interface" project.

Key experiences and outcomes include:

- Designed & manufactured a mechanical 3-axis calibrator for a live class-4 laser for Particle Image Velocimetry
  - Our setup works by shooting a laser to light up microscopic particles in our tank, and this helps us capture the fluid velocity as the fin flaps
  - Because our team was transitioning to image velocity from a different direction, the laser and camera both had to be moved
  - The calibrator I designed would help align this laser with the fin neutral position
- Processed 6-axis load cell data using MATLAB to quantify thrust generated by a biomimetic fish fin
- Programmed a PI-controlled rotational degree of freedom for the fin
  - Designed custom scaling op-amp circuits to provide feedback control with a potentiometer
  - Programmed and tuned a PI control feedback loop in C++
  - Troubleshot load cell/motor interference
- Managed waterjet safety & maintenance; advised team of 5 on machining processes to eliminate fin defects
